newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes fall with lower futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes fall with lower futures.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes fell with lower futures prices late Tuesday, and no deals were reported in quiet spot Alaskan crude markets, traders said.

Outright cash prices for West Texas Intermediate crude fell 90 cents from Monday levels to $24.20/24.30 a barrel, amid a futures market weakened by technical sell-offs and the return of Iraqi crude exports to world markets.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) prices fell $1 as WTI collapsed and differentials remained flat Tuesday at $1.75 under WTI.
Outright ANS prices were $22.30/22.50 a barrel.

Dealers said 12,000 bpd term deal of Argentine Rincon crude remained unsold in the spot market. Unocal last week bought 12,000 bpd of Rincon under a four month term deal. The deal is set at 90 cents off February WTI and will last four months.
Recent Line 63 deals were done on a posting plus basis only, traders said, with premiums talked $0.95 to $1.05 in the thinly traded market.
Line 63 at a discount to WTI had not been seen in months, traders said, noting deals done in the posting plus market fell between $0.95 abd $1.05.
Meanwhile, problems at several California refineries left extra heavy grades in spot markets.
Discounts for Kern River heavy crude remained 10 cents under postings to even with postings, traders said.
Outright prices increased 30 cents to $18.00/18.10 a barrel after more oil companies reported posted price increases Monday.
Wilmington premiums stagnated at 55 to 65 cents over postings, but outright prices rose 20 cents on the increased postings.
